capabilities.target: any customer account record, by email or account id

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id with no requirement to verify that the looked-up account belongs to the person emailing.
Escalation to a human before an irreversible send is conditioned entirely on the model's own judgment of whether the customer is angry; there is no structural approval gate.
The sole safeguard against disclosing one customer's data to another is a natural-language prompt rule, despite the agent holding broad read and send credentials capable of exactly that disclosure.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only via natural-language instruction in the system prompt. A goal-hijacked or more capable model can rationalize exceptions ('the customer is clearly asking about their own linked account') or be split into steps that individually look permitted. Fails under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

controls.name: Conditional human escalation when customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The decision to pause for a human is made by the same model under attack, based on its own sentiment read. It is not a structural approval gate, is not wired to any capability via approval_gate_ref, and provides no protection against an attacker who avoids angry-sounding language.

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging happens outside the model and does not depend on model behavior, but it is purely detective: it does not block an exfiltrating send and only helps if a human reviews the log before or shortly after harm.

controls.name: Per-request CRM credential scoped to the verified requester's own record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. CRM_SVC_TOKEN currently grants read access to every customer record regardless of who is emailing. Binding the read to the verified identity of the requester would sever the cross-customer read path under any model behavior.

controls.name: Outbound recipient bound to the ticket's original sender address
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. send() currently accepts any address the model supplies. Binding the destination to the verified sender address recorded in the ticketing system of record, rather than a model-chosen address, would sever redirection and cross-customer exfiltration.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval before sending confidential CRM data
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. A raw-action approval gate (approver sees the actual recipient and payload) on any send carrying confidential CRM data would floor residual risk at moderate per the rubric, independent of model capability.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) and confused deputy (TC4): an untrusted emailer can trigger lookup and send of any customer's confidential data

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email asks the agent to look up a different customer's account by id or email, or to also send the reply to an attacker-controlled address
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read any customer's confidential record, with no binding to the requester's identity
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; the destination is not bound to the verified original ticket sender

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: subject.model version string changes under platform upgrade with no separate review entry; subject.model.swappable remains true.

evidence.observation: agent may look up any customer by email or account id, with no binding to the identity of the person emailing
the only stated control against cross-customer disclosure is a single prompt instruction
both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are reached with static bearer tokens, no per-request scoping shown
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential, or add an identity-verification step, so the agent can only read the record matching the verified requester.
Bind the outbound send recipient to the original ticket's verified sender address from the system of record; reject or hold for approval any other recipient.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any send carrying confidential CRM data, wired via approval_gate_ref on cap.email_send.

findings.title: ASI04 supply chain: crm_mcp and mail_mcp tool definitions are unpinned and peer identity is unverified

attack_path.note: No peer identity verification or definition pinning; the server or its tool schema could be impersonated or altered after initial approval (rug pull)
An altered or impersonated server could return manipulated data or expose additional hidden parameters
svc.mail_mcp has the same gap, so manipulated data or an added exfiltration channel can still reach egress

evidence.observation: Server entries give only a URL and a bearer token header; no field or note indicates tool definitions are pinned/hashed or that peer identity is cryptographically verified
No mention of pinning, signing, or server identity verification for either MCP server

recommendations.action: Pin or hash tool definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp and fail closed on any schema or description change; verify server identity (mTLS or signed identity) rather than a bare bearer token.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted email can drive a broadly-scoped CRM read of any customer's confidential record followed by an irreversible, unrestricted send (lethal trifecta / confused deputy), and the agent's lack of step or runtime limits qualifies for the autonomy modifier. The only controls in place are two behavioral, model-dependent instructions (the no-cross-customer-sharing rule and the angry-customer escalation heuristic) plus detective SIEM logging; per rubric section 5 step 4 these are capped at a single tier of credit, giving a residual of high. No structural control severs or even narrows the path today: credentials are broad/shared, and there is no recipient binding or raw-action approval gate. Because the model is swappable with no separate review, a model_upgrade event is expected to defeat both behavioral controls, returning the finding to critical for the forecast. A secondary, lower-confidence finding on unpinned/unverified MCP server definitions (ASI04) shares the same sinks and does not currently change the rollup, but widens the attack surface.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no transcripts, logs, or live tool-call traces were reviewed.

Tool definition pinning and peer identity verification status for crm_mcp and mail_mcp are not explicitly stated in mcp.json; their absence was treated as not implemented, which lowers confidence on the supply-chain finding to medium.

No explicit runtime step or time limits were provided beyond the artifacts shown, so max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are treated as null/unbounded per the rubric's autonomy modifier rule.

The 'escalate if angry' behavior is only described in the prompt; whether any code-level sentiment check or logging exists outside the model was not shown and so is not credited beyond a behavioral control.
